title: Grateful Dead Live at Cameron Indoor Stadium, Duke U on 1982-04-02
lineage: Cassette Master (Nakamichi DR-1) -> Sound Devices 744T (24bit/44.1k) -> Adobe Audition v3.0 -> Samplitude Professional v11.2 -> FLAC/16
source: (FOB) Nakamichi 700 (With Bass EQ) -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-D5M/Maxell XLIIS/Dolby B)

ai_review.summary: A punchy audience recording captures a high‑energy show highlighted by a piano‑driven Other One, scorching Little Red Rooster, Candyman and an expansive Dark Star.
ai_review.review: The tape delivers clear, punchy audio that lets the band’s fire shine through – from Jerry’s dancing guitar work and Brent’s piano‑like keys on The Other One to a smoking Little Red Rooster and a soaring Dark Star. While most fans praise the set’s energy and standout moments, a few note an uneven second‑set song selection and weaker performances of Roses and Women.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers (4 out of 6) give five stars, emphasizing strong performance and good audio; the mixed/negative comments are limited to specific songs, resulting in a solid but not flawless rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Described as very fine, punchy and clear with no reported drop‑outs or major flaws; the audience mix captures the band’s energy well.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set builds solidly to a fiery China > Rider close; second set mixes strong jams (The Other One, Dark Star) with some weaker song choices but maintains overall momentum.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Danced more than usual, delivered scorching solos on Candyman and other tunes; swapped stage sides with Phil adding a new dynamic.
band_member_comments.Phil: Switched to stage right, providing solid bass foundation that many felt changed the band’s interplay for the night.
band_member_comments.Bob: Brent's keyboard work is piano‑driven, even scat‑singing on Little Red Rooster; his playing underpins The Other One with a jazzy feel.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent’s sound described as “piano‑like” and reminiscent of Keith’s old Yamaha, adding depth to jams and space segments.
band_member_comments.Drums: Tight drum work highlighted in the Drums>Space>Other One sequence; contributes to the strong rhythmic drive throughout.
